sources.name: Austin Water rainwater harvesting rebate
sources.summary: Austin Water lists a rainwater harvesting rebate of up to $5,000, based on system capacity.
sources.eligibility: Austin Water customers; confirm the current account and project requirements before buying equipment.
sources.application_requirements: Use the City of Austin Conservation Hub and confirm whether pre-approval is required.
sources.funding_status: Subject to current program rules and funding availability.

sources.name: Texas Water Development Board rainwater harvesting guidance
sources.summary: The Texas Water Development Board explains statewide tax and property-law provisions and publishes rainwater harvesting guidance.
sources.eligibility: Statewide guidance; local plumbing, health, and building rules may add requirements.
sources.application_requirements: Consult local authorities for permits and treatment requirements.
sources.funding_status: Guidance resource, not a rebate promise.

sources.name: SoCal Water$mart rain barrel and cistern rebates
sources.summary: SoCal Water$mart lists rain barrel and cistern rebates for customers of participating water agencies.
sources.eligibility: Customers of participating Southern California water agencies; rebate amounts vary by agency.
sources.application_requirements: Check the current program page and agency-specific terms before purchase.
sources.funding_status: Funding and available amounts vary by water agency and may change.

sources.name: Ley 91-2024: Ley para la Recolección y Cosecha de Agua de Lluvia en Puerto Rico
sources.summary: Ley 91-2024 (June 4, 2024) mandates rainwater collection systems on government buildings, creates a certified community-based rainwater harvesting program, and establishes rainwater harvesting as public policy for water security and hurricane resilience across Puerto Rico.
sources.eligibility: Government agencies required to install systems; communities may participate in certified program. Residential harvesting is legal and encouraged.
sources.application_requirements: Government agencies must implement per law timeline; community program certification details pending regulations.
sources.funding_status: Statutory mandate for government buildings; community program funding subject to legislative appropriation.

sources.name: Puerto Rico Plumbing Code 2018, Chapter 13 — Nonpotable Water Systems
sources.summary: The 2018 International Plumbing Code as adopted in Puerto Rico, Chapter 13 regulates rainwater collection and conveyance systems, nonpotable water systems for toilet flushing, irrigation, and on-site reuse, including storage tank requirements, filtration, and cross-connection control.
sources.eligibility: All rainwater systems plumbed for nonpotable indoor use must comply with Chapter 13 piping, storage, and backflow prevention requirements.
sources.application_requirements: Permits and inspections through OGPe (Oficina de Gerencia de Permisos); RPZ or air gap backflow prevention mandatory for municipal water connections.
sources.funding_status: Regulatory compliance standard, not a funding program.

sources.name: Puerto Rico Aqueduct and Sewer Authority (PRASA) Guidelines for Rainwater Systems
sources.summary: PRASA operates 97% of PR's public water supply; PRASA agreement revision and sanitary water meter installation are required when distributing harvested rainwater to indoor fixtures (toilets) per Keep Safe guide and PRASA interconnection requirements.
sources.eligibility: Property owners connecting rainwater systems to indoor plumbing must coordinate with PRASA for agreement revision and meter installation.
sources.service_territory: PRASA service territory (approx. 97% of Puerto Rico population)
sources.application_requirements: Submit PRASA agreement revision request; install sanitary water meter for indoor nonpotable distribution.
sources.funding_status: Regulatory interconnection requirement, not a funding program.
